cards.answer: Two pointers of different types (with exceptions such as `char*`) cannot point to the same memory location, so the compiler may reorder reads and writes across them.

cards.question: What is type punning?
cards.answer: Accessing a block of memory through a pointer of a different type or through a `union` to reinterpret its raw bit representation.

cards.question: What is a flexible array member (FAM)?
cards.answer: An unbounded array defined as the last member of a struct, such as `int data[]`. C99/C11/C17 use it to allocate dynamically sized structures in a single contiguous memory block.

cards.question: What do ASan and UBSan each detect?
cards.answer: AddressSanitizer (`-fsanitize=address`) instruments memory accesses to detect out-of-bounds accesses, use-after-free, double-free, and leaks. UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (`-fsanitize=undefined`) catches runtime UB such as signed integer overflow, null pointer dereference, and misaligned pointers.

cards.question: What implicit conversion did `-Wconversion` flag in `src/main.c`?
cards.answer: An implicit integer truncation where `SDL_Keycode` (a 32-bit integer) was assigned to `char` (an 8-bit integer).
cards.sourceTitle: LR-0003: CMake SDL2 Resolution & Integer Precision Diagnostics

cards.question: How did CMake resolve SDL2 headers on macOS and Linux?
cards.answer: Both `find_package(SDL2)` and a `pkg-config` fallback. On macOS this reached Homebrew headers at `/opt/homebrew/include/SDL2`.
cards.sourceTitle: LR-0003: CMake SDL2 Resolution & Integer Precision Diagnostics

cards.question: What integer-sizing rule follows from the truncation diagnostic?
cards.answer: Distinguish `int32_t`, `char`, and `uint8_t`, and avoid implicit narrowing casts.
cards.sourceTitle: LR-0003: CMake SDL2 Resolution & Integer Precision Diagnostics

cards.question: What return convention does `fseek` use?
cards.answer: The Unix status convention: `0` means success and non-zero means error.
cards.sourceTitle: LR-0004: Standard I/O Return Conventions & fread Parameters

cards.question: Why does `fread` separate `size` from `nmemb`?
cards.answer: `size` is the size of a single element and `nmemb` is the element count, which enables structured record-based reading.
cards.sourceTitle: LR-0004: Standard I/O Return Conventions & fread Parameters

cards.question: What does `fread` return?
cards.answer: The count of complete records transferred, not the raw byte count.
cards.sourceTitle: LR-0004: Standard I/O Return Conventions & fread Parameters

cards.question: What kind of release is C17 relative to C11?
cards.answer: C17 is the bug-fix and refinement release of C11. It introduced no new language features, but resolved over 40 technical defect reports.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0001: ISO C17 Standards, Compiler Diagnostics & CMake with SDL2

cards.question: What is the C17 value of `__STDC_VERSION__`?
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0001: ISO C17 Standards, Compiler Diagnostics & CMake with SDL2

cards.question: In C, how does `void foo()` differ from `void foo(void)`?
cards.answer: `void foo()` takes an unspecified number of arguments, a C89 leftover. `void foo(void)` declares a function that takes zero arguments.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0001: ISO C17 Standards, Compiler Diagnostics & CMake with SDL2

cards.question: Which compiler flag enforces empty-parameter prototypes?
cards.answer: `-Wstrict-prototypes`.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0001: ISO C17 Standards, Compiler Diagnostics & CMake with SDL2

cards.question: What does AddressSanitizer detect?
cards.answer: Buffer overflows, stack/heap out-of-bounds access, and memory leaks.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0001: ISO C17 Standards, Compiler Diagnostics & CMake with SDL2

cards.question: What does UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer detect at runtime?
cards.answer: Integer overflows, null-pointer dereferences, and misalignment.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0001: ISO C17 Standards, Compiler Diagnostics & CMake with SDL2

cards.question: How does CMake enforce ISO C17 without compiler extensions?
cards.answer: Set `CMAKE_C_STANDARD` to 17, `CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED` to `ON`, and `CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS` to `OFF`.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0001: ISO C17 Standards, Compiler Diagnostics & CMake with SDL2

cards.question: What is the runtime effect of `-fsanitize=address,undefined`?
cards.answer: It instruments memory reads/writes and arithmetic. Out-of-bounds writes, buffer overruns, or signed overflow halt the program with a stack trace instead of silently corrupting memory.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0001: ISO C17 Standards, Compiler Diagnostics & CMake with SDL2

cards.question: How much RAM does CHIP-8 address, and what is the range?
cards.answer: 4,096 bytes (4 KB), from `0x000` to `0xFFF`.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0002: Safe Binary File I/O & ROM Loading into Memory at 0x200

cards.question: Where must CHIP-8 ROMs be loaded, and where does the PC start?
cards.answer: ROMs load starting at `0x200`, and the program counter starts at `0x200`.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0002: Safe Binary File I/O & ROM Loading into Memory at 0x200

cards.question: What is the maximum CHIP-8 ROM size, and why?
cards.answer: 3,584 bytes (`4096 - 512`). A larger ROM overflows `memory.memory[4096]` and triggers undefined behavior.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0002: Safe Binary File I/O & ROM Loading into Memory at 0x200

cards.question: Why open ROM files with `"rb"` instead of `"r"`?
cards.answer: Text mode `"r"` can translate carriage returns (for example `\r\n` to `\n`) and silently corrupt binary bytes.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0002: Safe Binary File I/O & ROM Loading into Memory at 0x200

cards.question: What does `fopen` return if the file is missing or unreadable?
cards.answer: `NULL`.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0002: Safe Binary File I/O & ROM Loading into Memory at 0x200

cards.question: Why rewind after `fseek(..., SEEK_END)` and `ftell` before `fread`?
cards.answer: `fseek` to `SEEK_END` moves the file position to the end so `ftell` can report the byte offset. Without `rewind` or `fseek(..., SEEK_SET)`, `fread` would read from the end and get 0 bytes.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0002: Safe Binary File I/O & ROM Loading into Memory at 0x200

cards.question: Why is `sizeof(uint8_t)` 1, and why cast `file_size` to `size_t` for `fread`?
cards.answer: `uint8_t` is an exact 8-bit unsigned type of size 1. `ftell` returns a signed `long` that can be negative on error, while `fread` expects `size_t`. Check `file_size > 0` before the cast.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0002: Safe Binary File I/O & ROM Loading into Memory at 0x200

cards.question: What occupies `0x000`–`0x1FF` in this emulator?
cards.answer: That region historically held the CHIP-8 interpreter. Here the built-in 80-byte hexadecimal font set lives at `0x0000`–`0x0050`.
cards.sourceTitle: Lesson 0002: Safe Binary File I/O & ROM Loading into Memory at 0x200

cards.question: How large is CHIP-8 RAM, and what is its address range?
cards.answer: A 4KB RAM buffer from `0x000` to `0xFFF`.

cards.question: What registers does the CHIP-8 CPU expose?
cards.answer: 16 general-purpose 8-bit registers (`V0`–`VF`), a 16-bit index register `I`, the program counter `PC`, and delay/sound timers.

cards.question: How large is the CHIP-8 call stack?
cards.answer: A 16-level call stack with stack pointer `SP`.

cards.question: How is the CHIP-8 display represented?
cards.answer: A 64×32 2D boolean pixel matrix.

cards.question: How are 16-bit big-endian CHIP-8 instructions fetched?
cards.answer: `(mem[PC] << 8) | mem[PC + 1]`.

cards.question: Where should ROMs be loaded in CHIP-8 RAM?
cards.answer: At offset `0x200`.

cards.question: How do you enforce ISO C17 and disable extensions in CMake?
cards.answer: Set `CMAKE_C_STANDARD` to 17, `CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED` to `ON`, and `CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS` to `OFF`.
cards.sourceTitle: Modern C17 Toolchain and CMake Reference

cards.question: What does `CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS ON` provide?
cards.answer: It exports compile commands for clangd / LSP.
cards.sourceTitle: Modern C17 Toolchain and CMake Reference

cards.question: What does `-Wshadow` prevent?
cards.answer: Inner-scope variables hiding outer-scope variables.
cards.sourceTitle: Modern C17 Toolchain and CMake Reference

cards.question: What silent bug does `-Wconversion` catch?
cards.answer: Implicit type conversions that truncate, such as `uint64_t` into `uint32_t`.
cards.sourceTitle: Modern C17 Toolchain and CMake Reference

cards.question: Why is `-Wstrict-prototypes` required in C?
cards.answer: In C, `void foo()` means unspecified arguments; `void foo(void)` is required for a zero-argument function.
cards.sourceTitle: Modern C17 Toolchain and CMake Reference

cards.question: What runtime errors does `-fsanitize=address` catch?
cards.answer: Buffer overflows, use-after-free, and double-frees.
cards.sourceTitle: Modern C17 Toolchain and CMake Reference

cards.question: What runtime errors does `-fsanitize=undefined` catch?
cards.answer: Signed overflow, null pointer dereferencing, and alignment faults.
cards.sourceTitle: Modern C17 Toolchain and CMake Reference

cards.question: When does the CMake template enable ASan and UBSan?
cards.answer: When `ENABLE_SANITIZERS` is on and `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` matches Debug, using `-fsanitize=address,undefined`, `-fno-omit-frame-pointer`, and `-g`.
cards.sourceTitle: Modern C17 Toolchain and CMake Reference

cards.question: What are C's two standard-library return conventions?
cards.answer: Status/error code: `0` means success and non-zero means failure (`fseek`, `fclose`, `strcmp`). Value/count/handle: a valid object or count on success, `NULL` or `EOF` (`-1`) on failure (`fopen` returns `NULL`, `fread` returns items read, `ftell` returns `-1L`).
cards.sourceTitle: Standard I/O & Binary File Streams in C17

cards.question: How should you test `fseek` for failure under ISO C17?
cards.answer: `if (fseek(f, offset, origin) != 0)`. `fseek` returns nonzero on failure.
cards.sourceTitle: Standard I/O & Binary File Streams in C17

cards.question: What do `fread`'s `size` and `nmemb` parameters mean?
cards.answer: `size` is the size of a single element in bytes. `nmemb` is the number of elements to read.
cards.sourceTitle: Standard I/O & Binary File Streams in C17

cards.question: What does `fread` return?
cards.answer: The number of whole elements successfully read, not the raw byte count.
cards.sourceTitle: Standard I/O & Binary File Streams in C17

cards.question: If `fread` is asked for 10 `Player` structs and the file ends after 7 complete structs, what does it return?
cards.sourceTitle: Standard I/O & Binary File Streams in C17

cards.question: How do you measure file size and then read from the start?
cards.answer: `fseek(file, 0, SEEK_END)`, then `ftell(file)`, then `rewind(file)` (equivalent to `fseek(file, 0, SEEK_SET)`).
cards.sourceTitle: Standard I/O & Binary File Streams in C17

cards.question: Why is `"rb"` required for ROMs instead of `"r"`?
cards.answer: Binary mode reads raw bytes with no transformation. Text mode may translate newlines (for example `\r\n` to `\n`), which corrupts opcodes and shifts offsets.
cards.sourceTitle: Standard I/O & Binary File Streams in C17

cards.question: What is the relationship between `fread` bytes transferred, `size`, and `nmemb`?
cards.answer: Total bytes read equals `size` times `nmemb`.
cards.sourceTitle: Standard I/O & Binary File Streams in C17

cards.question: Where should you apply defensive validation of user input?
cards.answer: Do not trust user input. Put validators on form values and on the HTTP request body and query.

cards.question: Should you validate responses from backend services your own team manages?
cards.answer: No. If you need to be defensive against your own teammates' code, you have gone too far. Those validators introduce too many edge cases.

cards.question: If the backend returns a string instead of an array, should the frontend fall back to []?
cards.answer: No. The frontend should not validate that and fall back to an empty array. The UI can show an error via an error boundary, or simply break, because invariants have broken.

cards.question: Should the UI refuse to break no matter what?
cards.answer: No. Push back on the attitude that the UI must never break. If invariants have broken, the UI can show an error using an error boundary or simply break.

cards.question: What happens if you treat the backend as an antagonist to your code?
cards.answer: You will soon start to see the backend developers as antagonists to you.

cards.question: What is the real reason to extract a function, versus DRY reuse?
cards.answer: DRY is a decent starting rule, but the real reason to create, refactor to, or abstract to a function is to maintain local reasoning.

cards.question: What happens if you only extract a function when you need to reuse it?
cards.answer: You get a 300-line function. The same steps are not required anywhere else, so the function never gets split.

cards.question: Why are functions more for humans than for machines?
cards.answer: A human sees your code before a machine does. The CPU does not see functions; the compiler does extra work to turn them into instructions, managing return and parameter addresses and inlining where possible.

cards.question: How can DRY bloat a license-granting function?
cards.answer: Sales attach-on-behalf and anonymous checkout (create user if missing) get added to the same method because that is where users and licenses are linked. The function grows past 100 lines of if-checks that create different resources.

cards.question: When should you refactor for local reasoning, even with a single call site?
cards.answer: Refactor when you can reason about what a function does at a glance. Link-licenses-to-user should be its own function even if no other code calls it and it happens in only one spot.

cards.question: What should a link-licenses-to-user function take instead of IDs?
cards.answer: Valid user and license objects, not userId or licenseId. IDs would require validity checks; the function should just link them, even if the call is user.link(license).

cards.question: How does a bloated link flow violate Single Responsibility?
cards.answer: A function should have one reason to change. That link flow changes if user creation changes, and also if which products sales may link changes.

cards.question: What is LangGraph?
cards.answer: A specialized framework for building stateful, multi-actor applications with LLMs.

cards.question: What do cyclic and graph workflows enable?
cards.answer: Loops and conditional edges. That makes LangGraph a fit for ReAct loops, iterative refinement, and multi-agent debate.

cards.question: How does LangGraph manage state as execution moves?
cards.answer: It uses central state schemas that are updated deterministically as execution moves across graph nodes.

cards.question: What does human-in-the-loop support in LangGraph?
cards.answer: Pausing execution for human approval or feedback before resuming node transitions.

cards.question: What is time-travel debugging in LangGraph?
cards.answer: Rewinding state to inspect or fork execution paths during agent testing.
